transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I guess… I’ve just been feeling kind of foggy lately. At work I’m making small mistakes in my client notes, forgetting what I was about to do. It’s not really like me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yeah… I guess so. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling, like in my chest. I can still get through work and talk to people, but inside I just feel kind of sad. Flat.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but I haven’t really paid attention to it. I still do what I need to do.
Have you been feeling especially anxious or worried lately?
Not especially, no. I mean… normal stuff, I guess, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been more worried than usual.
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been paying that much attention to it, I guess. Some things feel a little muted, maybe, but… I still do them.
How have you been sleeping lately?
Not great, I guess. It’s kind of been all over the place… sometimes I’m just lying there thinking about family stuff, and other times I wake up before my alarm and can’t really get back to sleep.
How long have you been feeling this foggy and down?
I guess… about a month. It’s been kind of hanging over me that long, the foggy, low feeling.
Has something stressful been happening in your family lately?
Yeah… my uncle died about two weeks ago. I think that’s when this whole shift kind of started.
Did these foggy, low feelings start before your uncle died?
Yeah… I think it started before that. The low, foggy feeling’s been there maybe about a month now.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately?
Yeah… I have. Even when I haven’t really done much, I feel worn out. Little stuff at work, like helping someone shower, or even carrying groceries, feels like more than it should.
Have you noticed your appetite changing lately?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I haven’t been paying much attention to it.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
I’m not… planning to hurt myself or anything. But there’ve been a few mornings where I think maybe it wouldn’t be so bad if I just didn’t wake up. I don’t like that thought. It scares me.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
Yeah… a bit. My head’s been kind of foggy. I’ve been making small mistakes in my client notes, or I’ll walk into a room and forget what I was about to do. That’s not really like me.
Have you felt like your body or movements have been slowed down lately?
I don’t think so. I mean… I haven’t really noticed moving slower or anything like that.
Are your mood and energy usually worse in the morning?
Yeah… mornings are usually the hardest. I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I can still get through work and talk to people, but inside I just feel… sad. Flat.
Have you been getting less pleasure from things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I guess things haven’t felt as enjoyable lately, but I haven’t paid close attention to it.
Have you been eating less than usual lately?
I haven’t really noticed. My appetite seems… about the same, I guess.
In the past month, have you clearly lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know if I’d say clearly. Some things feel kind of muted, but I haven’t really been tracking it.
Have you been forgetting recent conversations or appointments more than usual?
Yeah… a bit. Mostly I feel kind of foggy. I’ve been forgetting what I was about to do, and I’ve made a few small mistakes in my client notes, which isn’t really like me.
Outside of this past month, were you having these memory or concentration problems before your mood started feeling low?
Not really before, no. It’s more what brought me in now… my head feels foggy, and I’ve been making little mistakes in my client notes or forgetting what I was about to do. That’s not really like me.

Cognitive complaints began with the mood episode rather than preceding it, supporting depressive syndrome over a primary memory disorder. Anxiety was not prominent, and although there was a recent bereavement/family stressor, symptoms started before the uncle's death, making an unspecified depressive episode the best fit among the candidates.
